newsitem.title: TURKEY: Allies give Turkey's Erbakan hours to quit - press.
newsitem.headline: Allies give Turkey's Erbakan hours to quit - press.

text.p: Turkey's junior coalition partner has given Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan until midnight on Wednesday to fulfil a promise to resign or face the immediate end of his government, Turkish newspapers said.

They quoted senior MP Mehmet Golhan as saying his True Path Party would pull out of the battered alliance if Erbakan did not hand in his resignation by the end of the day under a plan to transfer power to True Path leader Tansu Ciller.

"We have given (Erbakan's Welfare Party) until 2400 (2100 GMT). This is our last date and we will give no concessions on it. If Erbakan doesn't resign we will do what is needed," the Hurriyet daily quoted Golhan as saying.
True Path says Erbakan had previously agreed to step down on Wednesday and swap jobs with Deputy Prime Minister Ciller, who would head a caretaker government to take the country to early polls.

But Erbakan has so far ducked the issue of quitting. He did not mention resigning in an hour-long speech to his MPs on Tuesday. Erbakan would have to give his resignation to President Suleyman Demirel.
The president's office said on Wednesday there was as yet no meeting with the prime minister on the president's schedule.
The government, set up a year ago, has slowly been crumbling under pressure from the anti-Islamist military since February.
